topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Space Stage (1 Minute)
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation T(v) = Av as a 'mapping' that moves a vector from one space to another. Visualize this as a transformation of a 2D grid: space stretches, rotates, or shears.
sections.example: Visualize a cartoon character, 'Dot', sitting at coordinates (1,0). A matrix A acts as a magic 'stretching' machine.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition (1 Minute)
sections.content: Introduce the idea of sequential operations: first apply transformation B, then apply transformation A to the result. We write this as A(B(v)).
sections.example: Dot first gets 'rotated' by matrix B (a 90-degree turn), then the result gets 'scaled' by matrix A (doubling in size).

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Combined' Machine (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Explain that if A(B(v)) can be represented as a single new matrix C, then C = AB. This is the core insight: Matrix multiplication IS the process of collapsing two geometric steps into one single step.
sections.example: Show a dual-lens camera filter: Lens B distorts the image, then Lens A applies a color shift. The 'combined' lens C produces the exact same image in one go.

sections.title: The Calculation Rule (1 Minute)
sections.content: Demonstrate why we multiply rows by columns: the columns of the resulting matrix C represent where the original basis vectors (i and j) end up after the two-step journey.
sections.example: Trace the path of 'Dot' (1,0) through the two matrices. Calculate the final landing spot to reveal the first column of the product matrix.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Order Matters (0.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Highlight that AB ≠ BA. In geometric terms, rotating then scaling is not the same as scaling then rotating. End with a summary of matrix multiplication as the 'language of composed movement'.
sections.example: Use a character wearing a hat: 'Putting on a hat then a mask' vs 'Putting on a mask then a hat'—the final visual result is drastically different.
